question: In the Harappan civilisation, cire perdue or lost wax process was used to make statue of which material?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bronze**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The lost wax technique, also known as **cire perdue**, was used during the Harappan civilization for crafting **bronze statues**.
 
• One of the most famous examples is the **"Dancing Girl"**, a bronze figurine discovered at Mohenjo-Daro, showcasing the advanced metalworking skills of the Harappans.
 
• This technique involved creating a wax model, covering it with clay or another mold material, and then heating it so the wax melts and is replaced by molten metal.
 
• The process allowed for intricate designs and demonstrated the Harappans' mastery in metallurgy and art.
 
• The use of bronze highlights the significance of alloy-making and metal technology in the Harappan civilization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bronze:**

 
 
• Bronze is an alloy primarily consisting of copper and tin, known for its durability and corrosion resistance.
 
• It was widely used in ancient civilizations, including the Harappans, for making tools, weapons, and artistic objects.
 
• Bronze enabled the creation of detailed sculptures and was integral to trade and cultural exchange.
 
 
 
• **Lost Wax Technique (Cire Perdue):**
 
 
• The technique dates back thousands of years and is still used in modern sculpture-making.
 
• The process involves multiple steps, including creating a wax model, molding, and casting with metal.
 
• It allows for precision and intricate design, making it ideal for artistic expression.
 
 
 
• **Harappan Art and Craft:**
 
 
• The Harappan civilization was renowned for its craftsmanship in pottery, bead-making, metallurgy, and sculpture.
 
• The artifacts reflect their advanced skills, artistic sensibilities, and technological innovations.
 
• Materials like terracotta, stone, and metals were used extensively in their art and daily life.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Mohenjo-Daro:**
 
 
• Mohenjo-Daro is one of the largest settlements of the Indus Valley Civilization and a UNESCO World Heritage site.
 
• It has yielded numerous artifacts, including the famous "Dancing Girl" statue, which offers insight into Harappan culture.
 
• The site demonstrates the urban planning and artistic achievements of the civilization.
